title: How to Get Rich: Naval's framework on equity, specific knowledge, accountability, leverage and judgment
summary: Naval walks through his "How to Get Rich" tweetstorm line by line. Wealth comes from owning equity, building specific knowledge you can't be trained for, taking public accountability, applying permissionless leverage (code and media) with good judgment, and playing long-term games with high-integrity people.

principles.text: You can't get rich renting out your time; you need to own equity in a business, product or IP.
principles.quote: you're not going to get rich renting of your time you must own equity up piece of the business to gain your financial freedom

principles.text: Specific knowledge can't be taught in a class; it comes from your innate talents, curiosity and on-the-job apprenticeship.
principles.quote: the first thing to notice about specific knowledge is that you can't be trained for it

principles.text: Put your name on your work. Accountability earns you credibility, equity and leverage.
principles.quote: accountability is important because that's how you're going to get leverage that's how you're going to get credibility it's also how you're going to get equity

principles.text: The best modern leverage is permissionless: code and media with zero marginal cost of replication.
principles.quote: the most interesting and the most important form of leverage is this idea of products that have no marginal cost of replication this is the new form of leverage

principles.text: Once you have leverage, judgment is what compounds or destroys it, so build it through many iterations with skin in the game.
principles.quote: in an age of infinite leverage judgment becomes the most important skill

principles.text: Set an absurdly high personal hourly rate and outsource or skip anything that costs less than it.
principles.quote: set a very high hourly aspirational rate for yourself and stick to it and it should seem and feel absurdly high if it doesn't it's not high enough
